claim_register.claim: The SLA capacity page records daily volumes of 158,263 Trade, 173,610 Settlement GDC, and 3,898 ISO Korea, totaling 335,771. Peak assumptions are 19,396 Settlement, 10,927 Trade intraday, and 58,713 Trade EOD. Its heading leaves the hourly-versus-minute unit unresolved. Concurrent users change from 89 to 103 per minute; total users change from 386 to 545. The table gives targets of 77,584 Settlement and 43,708 Trade intraday per hour at four-times load. Trade EOD is 117,426 per hour at two-times load. Concurrent users are 412 at four-times load. The heading says four-times hourly capability, although the EOD row uses two-times. These are retained measurements or targets, without inspected test results.

claim_register.claim: The architecture test plan describes six VMs sharing business and infrastructure services across two data centers, plus two database nodes. It identifies resource shortage and poor fault isolation as risks. The proposed change adds six VMs, reorganizes microservices, and changes configuration. It calls for platform performance testing before production deployment. Acceptance preserves pre-upgrade service capability where a baseline exists, or relies on key-stakeholder belief that business requirements are met. This alternative is the retained proposal; it establishes no stakeholder approval.

claim_register.claim: The plan covers peak-load, endurance, and stress tests at 200%, 400%, 600%, and 800%, until performance targets fail. Volumes refer to a separate NFR document. Cases cover settlement Murex, Stella, suspended flows and BAU new; Trade Control Murex and FMRP; and FMO GUI. Cases run in parallel. Python generates backend traffic, mainly Kafka; JMeter simulates core APIs. Central Monitoring and ELK monitor execution. Increase load gradually from one-times to higher multiples, then clean test data and reset the environment. The retained plan contains no execution outcomes.
